summary:
HALO (Human Adaptation & Life Optimization) is an interactive psychological well-being support prototype designed for astronauts facing the challenges of isolation, confinement, and long-duration space missions.
Inspired by NASA's research on behavioral health and human performance, HALO provides a structured experience combining audiovisual journaling, supportive voice-based interviews, psychological check-ins, cognitive activities, and personalized well-being suggestions.
The platform explores five key dimensions: stress, sleep difficulties, interpersonal conflict, loneliness, and mental fatigue. It also includes gamified wellness activities, longitudinal progress charts, color-coded indicators, and an interactive 3D astronaut visualization that helps users understand changes in their well-being.
HALO adapts its experience to three mission environments: orbital stations, interplanetary transit, and lunar habitats.
By making psychological self-reflection more accessible and engaging, HALO aims to support astronaut resilience and encourage timely awareness of well-being concerns. It is an educational prototype, not a validated clinical diagnostic system.
details:
HALO (Human Adaptation & Life Optimization) is a web-based psychological well-being support prototype developed to explore how digital tools could assist astronauts during prolonged space missions.

Space exploration presents unique challenges, including isolation, confinement, demanding workloads, disrupted sleep schedules, and limited communication with Earth. HALO responds to these challenges by providing an accessible environment for self-reflection, structured monitoring, cognitive engagement, and supportive guidance.

How HALO Works

The astronaut begins by selecting one of three mission scenarios: an orbital space station, interplanetary transit, or a lunar surface habitat.

After reviewing privacy and consent information, the astronaut can participate in an audiovisual diary, sharing personal experiences without interruption. HALO then offers a supportive interview with follow-up questions informed by the topics identified during the interaction.

The prototype combines this process with structured check-ins covering five psychological dimensions:

- Stress

- Sleep difficulties

- Interpersonal conflict

- Loneliness and isolation

- Mental fatigue

HALO also includes cognitive mini-activities inspired by research on attention, reaction time, and cognitive performance in spaceflight.

Interactive Well-being Support

Based on the information entered during a session, the application presents descriptive summaries and suggested well-being activities, including relaxation exercises, reflection, and supportive routines.

A gamification system encourages participation in healthy habits through challenges, progress tracking, and achievement badges.

To improve the understanding of longitudinal information, HALO includes interactive graphs that display changes across sessions, as well as color-coded indicators designed to make trends easier to interpret.

An additional 3D Well-being Explorer provides an interactive astronaut model alongside psychological indicators and their explanations. This feature translates numerical information into a more accessible visual experience.

Technical Development

HALO was developed as a modular web prototype using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

The application incorporates browser-based camera and microphone functionality, speech recognition and speech synthesis where supported, interactive visualizations, and local session storage.

Its architecture separates the user interface, audiovisual interaction, psychological questions, cognitive activities, progress visualization, and application navigation into maintainable modules.

The conversational prototype currently uses adaptive rules and predefined follow-up logic. It is not presented as a fully autonomous clinical AI system.

Innovation and Creativity

HALO combines several components in a unified astronaut-centered experience:

- Mission-specific psychological support scenarios

- Audiovisual self-reflection and conversational guidance

- Cognitive activities and structured psychological check-ins

- Gamified wellness practices

- Longitudinal progress visualization

- An interactive 3D astronaut model

- Zambi, a companion inspired by the Junín grebe, a bird associated with life in a geographically restricted environment

Rather than focusing exclusively on physical performance, HALO emphasizes the human experience of space exploration.

Intended Impact

The aims to encourage self-awareness, support positive well-being habits, and help astronauts recognize changes in their psychological experiences over time.

The prototype is intended to complement, not replace, professional behavioral health services.

Its questionnaires, visual thresholds, and cognitive mini-activities have not been independently clinically validated. Future development would require expert evaluation, stronger data protection, usability testing, and validation in relevant research environments.

Our long-term vision is to contribute to a future in which psychological well-being receives the same attention as other essential aspects of astronaut health and mission readiness.
